source.title: Open problems and some results on strongly closed subalgebras of B(X)

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex locally convex topological vector space and let A be a complex algebra. A representation T of A on X is irreducible when no proper closed subspace of X is invariant under all representing operators T_a; it is n-fold irreducible when every n-tuple of linearly independent vectors has dense orbit in X^n under the diagonal action; and it is totally irreducible when it is n-fold irreducible for every natural number n. If T is irreducible and its commutant {S in L(X): S T_a = T_a S for every a in A} consists only of scalar multiples of the identity operator, must T be totally irreducible?

evidence.quote: A representation T is said to be totally irreducible, if it is n -fold irreducible for all n .
Does it follow that T is totally irreducible?

accepted.question_text: Let H be a complex Hilbert space and let B(H) be the algebra of bounded linear operators on H. Suppose A is a strongly closed subalgebra of B(H) that is transitive, meaning that A has no proper closed invariant subspace, equivalently all nonzero vector orbits under A are dense in H. Must A coincide with B(H)?

evidence.quote: The Transitive Algebra Problem is the question whether
for a complex Hilbert space H a strongly closed transitive subalgebra of B{H) must coincide with B(H) .

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space and let B(X) be the algebra of bounded linear operators on X. For a closed subspace M of X^n in general position, define A(M) to be the set of operators T in B(X) such that (x_1,...,x_n) in M implies (T x_1,...,T x_n) in M. A proper strongly closed subalgebra A of B(X) is of order n if A is contained in some such A(M) over X^n and is not contained in any such construction over X^k for k<n; an m.s.c.a. is a maximal strongly closed algebra. If A is any proper strongly closed subalgebra of B(X), must A be contained in some m.s.c.a., and more specifically in some m.s.c.a. of the same order as A?
accepted.context_brief: Containment in maximal strongly closed algebras

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Let A be a proper strongly closed subalgebra of B(X) , is it contained in some m.s.c.a. (or in some m.s.c.a. of the same order) ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Banach space X such that B(X), the algebra of bounded linear operators on X, has proper strongly closed subalgebras of arbitrarily high orders, where order is the notion for strongly closed subalgebras defined by containment in A(M) for a closed subspace M of X^n in general position and failure of such containment for all lower powers X^k?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Does there exist a Banach space X such that B(X) has subalgebras of arbitrarily high orders ?

accepted.question_text: For every natural number n, does there exist some Banach space X such that B(X), the algebra of bounded linear operators on X, has a proper strongly closed subalgebra of order n, with order understood via the A(M) construction over X^n and noncontainment in lower-order A(M) constructions?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Does there exist a Banach space X for each natural number n such that B(X) has a subalgebra of order n ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Banach space X such that B(X), the algebra of bounded linear operators on X, has a proper strongly closed subalgebra of order 3, in the sense of the order notion for strongly closed subalgebras defined via the A(M) construction?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Does there exist a Banach space X such that B(X) has a subalgebra of order 3 ?
